Yes Section 2: CANDIDATE EXPERIENCE (Short Answer) Please provide brief responses to each of the following questions - cite specific examples of your policy proposals and/or previous actions as applicable. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBT civil rights movement. I am committed to fighting for equality and dignity for all New Yorkers. In New York State, when the Democrats took control of the New York State Senate for the first real time in almost 100 years, we made significant strides in establishing basic protections for the LGBT community. First and foremost, we passed GENDA to prohibit discrimination on the basis of gender identity or expression and included gender identity and expression under hate crime law. GENDA was especially important because we added Transgender New Yorkers to those protected by the state’s Hate Crime Laws. In addition to passing GENDA, we passed a ban on conversion therapy,which was the morally and ethically next right thing to do, prohibiting mental health professionals from engaging in sexual orientation change efforts with a patient under the age of eighteen. These are basic protections, but they are a serious matter of acknowledging the humanity and dignity of all LGBT individuals. Moreover, we finally eliminated the “gay panic” defense, which which let murderers claim temporary insanity because they found out someone was gay or

[PDF page 40] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses transgender (S.6573 / Hoylman;) and made it possible for veterans who were discharged under Don’t Ask Don’t Tell to be eligible for veterans’ benefits (S.45B / Hoylman). I also am advocating for including a third gender option on state documents. What experience do you have to demonstrate you are the best person to represent the office you seek? As the democratic incumbent for the 34th state senate district, representing the Bronx & Westchester in Albany for the past 14 months, I realize that the most important core value that I carry with me into every meeting, event, and session on the floor is integrity and transparency. We have failed in almost every category when it comes to putting New Yorkers first. If we actually want to earn the title of public servants, we must start serving the public instead of the special interests who have been given the key to the castle for far too long. Yes, we’ve made progress on LGBT issues, housing issues, criminal justice reform, immigration issues, election reform, reproductive rights, sexual harassment, assault and rape laws, however, let us not be jaded or blinded by the progress we’ve made. Progress that was stalled for a decade, and progress that only brought us “current” so to speak. As we look towards the future, it is incumbent upon us to have a collective vision that brings New York forward, and let’s New York lead to its fullest potential. To do so requires embracing technology and the future of work, upending racism, sexism, and homophobia. Becoming a state where all zip codes are desirable to live in because the air is clean and the schools are good. Sure. We have made progress, but we have not taken the necessary step forward to lead. I am running for re-election to continue the work I have set out to accomplish in the New York State Senate, and to see the above mentioned vision to fruition. My desire to serve and my dedication to do what is right and just has only grown more deeply in my 14 months serving; and as Chairwoman of the Ethics Committee, my work is certainly far from done. I believe that our time as legislators is precious. We have an unknown amount of time serving, just like we have an unknown amount of time on this earth. That means that every issue I stand by, and every issue I fight for, is done with intense passion and urgency, because no one knows what tomorrow will bring. While serving, I have experienced some of the most disappointing days in my life -- but these days have often been followed by utter inspiration, motivation and a fervor to break down the walls erected to keep certain people, ideas, and laws alive. I believe these walls were made to be taken down by me, and my commitment to justice and a world that is equally accessible to everyone, has only grown stronger and louder during this time.

[PDF page 41] 2020 State Candidate Questionnaire Responses As a representative of the Bronx, I have witnessed devastating poverty, homelessness, overdose rates, and an underinvestment in its neighborhoods and its future, across almost every single categorical vertical that exists (education, job growth, health care, housing). I have seen people of color arrested on offenses that in other communities would be written off as a warning. I have witnessed survivors of human trafficking, transforming their pain to fight to save the young women being trafficked in the Bronx. I have watched as corporations set up shop in the posh streets of “SoBro”, or the South Bronx, only to take more from the people who have been given the least -- only to drive a thousand more trucks on their streets and make their air more likely to cause them asthma and in some cases, death. I have experienced our healthcare system being torn down during a pandemic, not because we were not prepared as a city or a state, but because cuts were made to “save money” in the areas that had the most need. This behavior and so much more, keeps me fighting for every single resident of District 34, and keeps me focused on the progress that we must make. I still also believe in FDR’s Four Freedoms -- freedom of speech and expression, freedom of religion, freedom from want, and freedom from fear -- and that these freedoms clearly define the bedrock principles of progressivism. These principles call us to ensure access to housing, healthcare, education, safety in our communities, self-determination, and more for every single human being. Applied today, I would include ending the politics of exclusion; harnessing the potential power of government for the good of all; and eliminating the outsized influence of money and corporate interests in campaigning and in the creation and passage of public policies.
